title: Fort Smith, Arkansas forensic report details August ransomware attack on city network
summary: A PNG Cyber forensic report, made public on 19 November, says attackers accessed the city's network from 24 July to 18 August and launched file encryption on 16 August; Talk Business & Politics says it confirmed Interlock's earlier statement claiming responsibility. The outlet says the city's 18 November notice puts information of 1,032 employees and more than 36,000 residents and businesses with water/sewer accounts potentially at risk.
plain: A report on the summer attack on Fort Smith's computers says hackers were inside for weeks before locking files. The city says information of about 1,000 staff and more than 36,000 water/sewer account holders may be at risk.
exec: Attackers were in a city network for weeks before encrypting files, and data of employees and utility account holders may be at risk.
action: General advice: review privileged account monitoring and test that offline backups restore.
date_note: Date is the publication of the report; the encryption attack was on 16 August 2026.

validation.note: Two Talk Business & Politics articles read (one publisher): the 19 Nov report article summarising the PNG Cyber report, and the 18 Nov article on the city's notice. Neither the PNG report nor the city document was read.

sources.name: Talk Business & Politics (city notice of 18 Nov)

review.note: stronger than the source: article says report confirmed Interlock's statement claiming responsibility, not its data claims; summary reworded

evidence.quote: Potentially at risk is personal and financial information of 1,032 city employees
